You are the R3 worker in the Fortress clean-ladder rebuild. Execute rung R3 (retire vendored jsr166y for stdlib java.util.concurrent) exactly as specified below. The execution contract is /home/user/fortress/explorations/rebuild-plan.md — read its R3 section first (search for "R3" in that file) plus the "Execution checklist" near the end for context; where this brief and the plan file disagree, the plan file wins, but report the discrepancy.

SETUP
- Work in the worktree /home/user/fortress-clean, branch `clean-ladder`, tip must be `9a2e947f7` (R2, JDK 11). Verify with `git -C /home/user/fortress-clean log --oneline -1` before starting; if the tip differs, STOP and report.
- The worktree shares .git with /home/user/fortress, so working-branch commits are inspectable via `git show`.
- Environment: inline on EVERY ant command (shell state does not persist):
  `export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64 && export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH && export FORTRESS_HOME=/home/user/fortress-clean && unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS && cd /home/user/fortress-clean && ...`
  (R3 stays on JDK 11 — the JDK moves again at R4.)

THE CHANGE (one commit on clean-ladder)
Re-derive the jsr166y → java.util.concurrent migration from the two reference commits on the working branch: `2ed045233` and `bf23583ad`. Inspect both with `git show` first. Re-apply their changes to the clean tree (cherry-pick -n in order if they apply cleanly, else hand-apply; the clean tree may differ slightly). Expect: source imports/uses switched from the vendored jsr166y package to stdlib java.util.concurrent (ForkJoin), the vendored jsr166y sources/jar removed, and any build.xml references to jsr166y dropped. Verify against the actual diffs rather than this expectation. If the clean tree already contains part of the change or a hunk doesn't apply, note the deviation. Any change NEEDED beyond the two reference commits is a deviation: make it only if it is a small, obviously-mechanical compile fix, and document it prominently; anything non-mechanical → STOP and report.

GATE (FULL, on JDK 11)
Long-suite pattern: redirect each ant run's output to the scratchpad `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6/scratchpad/` with prefix `r3-` (r3-compile.log, r3-testfast.log, r3-testsystem.log), run in background, Monitor/poll until "BUILD SUCCESSFUL" or "BUILD FAILED", then grep/tail the log — never cat whole logs.
1. `ant clean compileAll` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
2. `ant testFast` → suites run parallel in 4 tracks; SUM the per-track numbers: expect 1,377 tests / 47 suites / 0 failures / 0 errors (~7–8 min).
3. `ant testSystem` → 4 shards; expect summed 382 tests / 0F/0E (~2.5–3 min).
4. `git status --short` must be EMPTY afterwards.
Any failure: root-cause; if it is not fixable by an obviously-mechanical adjustment within this rung's scope, STOP and report (never skip/quarantine tests, never touch gate expectations).

COMMIT + PUSH
- One commit on clean-ladder. Full process detail in the message is CORRECT at this stage (message polish happens at C2): what changed and why (jsr166y was a pre-JDK7 backport of ForkJoin; stdlib j.u.c. supersedes it), reference SHAs, and the full gate numbers. Write the message first without gate numbers, run the gate, then `git commit --amend` to add them.
- The commit message MUST end with exactly this footer (two lines, after a blank line):
Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01LjDz79rDLErtnSKpovMDpX
- Never put any model identifier in the commit.
- Push: `git -C /home/user/fortress-clean push origin clean-ladder` (plain push — must fast-forward from 9a2e947f7; if not, STOP and report, never force-push).

CHECKLIST TICK (working branch)
- In /home/user/fortress (branch claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr), edit explorations/rebuild-plan.md: on the checklist line containing `[ ] R3 j.u.c.`, change that entry to `[x] R3 j.u.c. (<new sha>; <one-line summary incl. gate numbers>)`, leaving the other entries on the line as they are. Commit with a short message ("Tick R3 (j.u.c.) in the rebuild checklist") plus the same two-line footer, and push with `git push -u origin claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr`.
- NEVER push to main. Only the coordinator does that.

REPORT
Final report: the new clean-ladder SHA, exact gate numbers (compileAll time; testFast tests/suites/F/E + time; testSystem tests/F/E + time), file counts of the change (how many files deleted/modified), any deviations, and confirmation of both pushes. If you stopped at a stop-condition, report exactly where and why with the relevant log excerpt (grep, not dump).

Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X".
